i1.name: Clean Slate
i1.big: Every Dominion page thrown out and rebuilt as a modern Pokémon menu: rounded panels with white borders, a real Pokémon text box, HP-style stat bars, and Nova crimson for what is chosen.

1.name: Rebuilt from the ground
1.big: All 50 pages redrawn from scratch in one clean Pokémon menu language. Lists on the left, details on the right, a real text box for every talk.
1.q1: Big Jersey titles, a crimson glow on whatever is chosen, every panel springs in, the dial on the Card fills, stamps slam on results.
1.q2: Round 4 had a different layout on every screen. Now every page shares one grammar (top bar, list, detail, key strip), so the player learns it once.
1.q3: Not yet; this pass sets the base. Pages already split: Assign, District file, Card, Order cut-in, results.
1.q4: Esc opens the Boss Menu from any page; Settings has its own tabs (Dominion, Rotom, Effects, Sound).
1.q5: Yes: Pokémon-style text box with the ▼ arrow, HP bars for stats, a PC-box Reserve, a real battle screen.

2.name: Split the clutter
2.big: The HQ was one crowded screen. Now each floor opens its own page, plots are bought on a page of their own, and Kice's new Auto-Checker gets a desk page and a weekly report.
2.q1: A gold 'Lv 4 ready' badge pulses on the HQ; the level-up page stamps NEW FLOOR in huge letters.
2.q2: Pass 1 crammed rooms, plots and hiring into one panel. Now each one is a page with room to breathe, and lists show a breadcrumb so you always know where you are.
2.q3: Yes: five new HQ pages (floor, plot, Auto-Checker, hire report, level up). The HQ itself only shows the building and today's orders.
2.q4: The breadcrumb starts from the Boss Menu's section names (HQ, Crew, Map), so the menu and the pages use the same words.
2.q5: Buying a plot reads like a Poké Mart list; the Auto-Checker report is laid out like a PC box of new faces.

3.name: Everything morphs
3.big: Moving between pages is now one motion: the title, money, Heat, portraits and the chosen district fly to where they sit on the next page, and a crimson blade with the Nova eye wipes the rest. Two more pages split off.
3.q1: A crimson blade sweeps across every page change; portraits glide from the Morning list into the Crew File instead of popping.
3.q2: Pass 2 pages appeared and vanished. Now nothing pops: every shared part morphs, so the player sees where they came from.
3.q3: Build a room (after buying a plot) and Give a Pokémon (from the Reserve) are now pages, not pop-ups.
3.q4: The wheel and the Boss Menu use the same blade, so opening a menu feels like the same world, not a separate overlay.
3.q5: The wipe is a Pokémon-style battle transition in Nova colours; the Give page reads like the party-select screen.

4.name: Menu and Settings grow up
4.big: Every Settings tab is its own page (Dominion, Rotom, Effects, Sound) and every Boss Menu choice opens a full page: Save and quit, Controls and Replay a lesson are new.
4.q1: Settings rows slide in one by one with pill switches; the save slots are big letter cards.
4.q2: Pass 3 had Settings as one crowded list and Save as a single menu line. Now each is a full page, reached in one press from the Boss Menu.
4.q3: Five new pages. Effects has its own page so 'Full show, Lighter, Calm' is easy to find.
4.q4: This is the pass for it: Boss Menu (9 choices) → each choice is a page; Settings tabs are pages that morph into each other.
4.q5: The save page copies Pokémon's 'Save your progress?' slots; the Controls page reads like the in-game Help.

5.name: Spectacle
5.big: The first real show: coins rain on every win, sirens and police tape on every botch, speed lines and a shake on VS, light rays and a pulse ring behind Mega, Dynamax, Tera and Z, searchlights on the title. Rotom's lesson pop-up is drawn for the tutorial.
5.q1: Much more: every result and cut-in now has a moving background layer, and the title sweeps searchlights over the city.
5.q2: Pass 4 was tidy but still. Now each page type has its own signature motion, all of it on the background or the Pokémon, never on moves.
5.q3: Rotom's lessons get their own overlay page that dims everything but the part being taught.
5.q4: Effects (pass 4) has a 'Calm' switch that stops all of this; every animation also stops under reduced motion.
5.q5: Light rays behind a Mega are straight from the games; the battle transition shake and VS speed lines feel like a Gym Leader intro.

i2.name: Comic Caper
i2.big: Interval 1 is thrown away. Dominion becomes a Saturday-morning villain comic: thick ink borders, halftone dots, slanted panels, yellow caption boxes, speech balloons and sound-effect lettering. Each page is a comic page of two to four panels.

6.name: Issue #18
6.big: Every page redrawn as a comic page. The top bar is the issue masthead with a price tag for your money and a striped Heat gauge. Talks are two slanted panels and a balloon; results are a white burst with KA-CHING! or BUSTED!
6.q1: Far louder: sunburst backgrounds, sound effects that boom in, buttons that jig like stickers, every panel slaps down at an angle.
6.q2: Pass 5 was a clean, calm menu. This pass changes everything: colour, type, layout and motion all come from comics, and every page reads as a story beat.
6.q3: Not yet; the comic look is being set across the same 76 pages first.
6.q4: The Boss Menu is the comic's cover page: the Boss in his own panel with a balloon, the choices in a tall panel. Settings tabs are skewed comic tabs.
6.q5: Yes: it is how Team Rocket feels in the anime, a cartoon villain gang. The battle, PC box and text box keep their Pokémon shape inside the comic frame.

7.name: Chapters
7.big: Each day now opens with a chapter cover (title, the job, the Hero lurking in shadow). Heat gets a Wanted poster page that says what each level brings. Crew banter plays as a three-panel strip.
7.q1: The chapter cover spins sun rays behind a giant title; the Hero's silhouette fades in last as a cliffhanger.
7.q2: Pass 6 drew the same pages in comic style. Pass 7 uses the comic form to tell the day as a story: chapter, poster, strip.
7.q3: Yes: three pages that used to be lines of text (the new day, the Heat number, Rotom's chatter).
7.q4: The Wanted poster's button 'Lie low!' is the same action as the Boss Menu's Heat tip, so both lead to the morning.
7.q5: The Wanted poster is pure Team Rocket; chapter covers feel like the anime's episode title cards.

8.name: Reading order
8.big: Pages now play in reading order: panels land one after another, speech balloons write themselves in, sound effects wobble. Events split into three pages (the text, then the choice, then the reward), and Continue opens with a 'Previously on' recap.
8.q1: Every page now has a little sequence instead of one flash, so the eye is led panel to panel like a comic.
8.q2: Pass 7 still dropped every panel at once. Now order matters, and long event text has room because the choices moved to their own page.
8.q3: Yes: the event choice is its own page (the text stays until you press a key, then the choices), and the recap is a page on Continue.
8.q4: The recap can be skipped with Esc; Settings › Effects › Text speed sets how fast balloons write in.
8.q5: Event text works like a Pokémon NPC talk: text first, then a choice box, reward only after the text is closed.

9.name: Splash pages
9.big: The biggest moments drop their panels and take the whole page, like a comic splash: battle intros, the Boss's order, aces, Mega, Dynamax, Tera, Z-Power, the Betrayal and a new Rocket raid on your HQ. Giant italic words (VS!, MEGA!, Z-POWER!) slam in over spinning speed lines.
9.q1: The splash pages are the loudest yet: full-page speed lines, a black ink slash between the two sides, the Pokémon growing in with a flash of light.
9.q2: Pass 8 put big moments in the same two panels as a chat. Now quiet talks and big moments look different, so the player feels the difference.
9.q3: The Rocket raid on the HQ is now a page with three choices (defend, run with the Vault, pay off) instead of a morning line.
9.q4: Settings › Effects › Screen shake and Flashes control the splash moments only.
9.q5: Gym Leader intros and Mega Evolution in the games use this exact beat: two sides, a slash, a shout. Only the Pokémon and background move; no move animation changes.

10.name: Extras
10.big: The comic's back pages become real menus: a Mailbag of letters from visitors and rivals (Favours and Grudges you can call in) and a Cover gallery of your past runs. Settings gets a live preview panel showing what each choice looks like. The Boss Menu now has 11 choices, each a page.
10.q1: Settings shows a moving MEGA! preview, so 'Full show' versus 'Calm' is seen, not guessed.
10.q2: Pass 9 made the moments loud; pass 10 makes the quiet parts (letters, past runs, settings) worth opening too.
10.q3: Two new pages. Favours and Grudges used to be hidden numbers; now they arrive as letters you can act on.
10.q4: The Boss Menu lists everything (HQ, Crew, Pokémon, Map, Ledger, Mailbag, Rotom, Covers, Lessons, Settings, Save), each a single press away; nothing opens a menu inside a menu.
10.q5: The mailbag is the PC's Mail box; the cover gallery is the Hall of Fame for villains.
